narrative:
The model estimated a 66% chance that you will leave your job, meaning leaving is more likely than staying. Because retention risk is elevated, the promotion decision was denied.

The strongest influence was your overall work experience: being in the 1–5 year range—the most common range among employees predicted to stay, at about half—pushed the prediction toward staying and lowered your leaving risk. The next strongest factor was outside job opportunities. You indicated yes, while only about 23% of employees predicted to stay had other opportunities, so this sharply pushed toward leaving. Your sector, “other,” was third; because only about 22% of stay-predicted employees were in that sector, it modestly increased leaving risk. In combination, the stabilizing effect of your early-career experience was outweighed by external opportunities and sector context, producing the 66% leaving estimate.

What to consider next: the organization should discuss your career path, internal mobility, and concrete retention steps, since external opportunities are the clearest risk signal. You should also clarify promotion criteria and whether your current role can match the alternatives you see outside.
